qualification_this_checkpoint.input_domain: Finite rational residuals r > -1, representing ln(1+r), optionally plus shift*ln(2), with uncancelled evaluation and supported precision/resource limits. Existing invalid-residual import rejection is preserved. General native domains and fallible evaluation remain separate obligations.
qualification_this_checkpoint.next: Continue scalar domain/evidence ownership and ordinary strict completion, then complete the shipped user path and release validation.
qualification_this_checkpoint.proof_argument: Zero is exact. For a nonzero residual, an affirmative exact binary magnitude below -1 proves |r| < 1/2. Then 1/2 < 1+r < 3/2, so |ln(1+r)| < ln(2) < 1, justifying the coarse-zero shortcut and the existing series/error budget. Missing magnitude metadata is not a smallness proof. Otherwise r.add_one() forms the exact positive logarithm argument, and the existing native logarithm reducer computes the same value. The binary-scaled kernel retains its original two-term precision budget but now receives a valid approximation of its residual logarithm. No wrapper normalization or stored-graph mutation is used.
